uk-cpi-2026-10.standing: The Office for National Statistics' monthly measure of how fast prices are rising for UK households. The Bank of England targets it at 2%, so it steers interest rates, and benefit and pension increases are tied to it.
uk-cpi-2026-10.recent: Economists have warned of 5% UK inflation if a US diesel ban goes ahead, which turns attention to the fuel and energy lines of this release rather than the headline rate alone. The September figure reports prices as they stood while that ban was still a proposal, and it sets the baseline the warning is measured against.

fomc-2026-10.standing: The Federal Reserve's rate-setting committee, which meets eight times a year to set the federal funds rate. That rate anchors borrowing costs across the US economy and, through the dollar, the price of credit worldwide.
fomc-2026-10.recent: Hiring stalled in September at 29,000 jobs against 90,000 expected, which sets a weakening labour market against the four rate hikes traders had priced in by June 2027. Powell leads the meeting weeks after Trump demanded his resignation, and while Fed officials question JPMorgan, Wells Fargo and other banks on their private credit lending.

ecb-2026-10.standing: The European Central Bank's Governing Council, which meets eight times a year to set rates for the countries that share the euro. Its decisions reach borrowing costs for some 350 million people, and the euro moves with them.
ecb-2026-10.recent: Euro zone inflation jumped to 3.8% in September from 3.2%, the highest in three years, days after Lagarde painted a darkening picture of prices in Europe. Business activity is at a 3½-year high at the same time, so rate-setters cannot read the jump as the product of a weak economy; this meeting settles whether they answer it with a hike.

boj-2026-10.standing: Japan's central bank, whose policy board meets eight times a year to set the short-term interest rate. Its rate has long been the lowest of any major economy, so its moves reach the yen and everyone worldwide who borrows in it.
boj-2026-10.recent: Three sources told Reuters the bank may say this month that underlying inflation has roughly reached its 2% target. For a decade it justified near-zero rates by arguing that inflation was still short of that mark, so dropping the line removes its own stated reason to hold. At stake is the yen, which cheap Japanese rates have held down.

boe-2026-11.standing: The Bank of England's nine-member Monetary Policy Committee, which meets eight times a year to set Bank Rate. Its vote feeds through to UK mortgage and savings rates, and sterling and gilt yields move with it.
boe-2026-11.recent: The committee votes on whether to move the rate that the country's mortgages, savings accounts and business loans are priced from. Nothing reported so far sets this meeting apart from a routine one.

fomc-2026-12.standing: The Federal Reserve's rate-setting committee, which meets eight times a year to set the target for overnight lending between US banks. Its decisions move borrowing costs worldwide, since most global debt is priced off the dollar.
fomc-2026-12.recent: Hiring stalled in September — 29,000 new US jobs against 90,000 expected — while the committee is still weighing rate hikes, so the two halves of its mandate pull opposite ways. It decides with Trump demanding Powell resign, and with Fed officials questioning banks about loans to private credit firms that higher rates make harder to carry.

g20-2026-miami.standing: The yearly meeting of leaders from 19 major economies plus the European Union and African Union, hosted by a rotating presidency that sets the agenda. Its members produce about 85% of world output, and it decides by consensus.
g20-2026-miami.recent: Rubio has invited Putin, who is wanted by the ICC, to Miami, and the Kremlin is weighing the invitation. Its answer sets what the summit is about before any agenda item: whether the other leaders sit at a table with him, and whether a host's invitation counts for more than the court's.

ecb-2026-12.standing: The European Central Bank's Governing Council, which meets roughly every six weeks to set interest rates for the countries sharing the euro. Its deposit rate reaches mortgages, business loans and the euro's exchange rate.
ecb-2026-12.recent: Euro zone inflation jumped to 3.8% in September, the highest in three years, and Lagarde has painted a darkening picture of prices in Europe. Business activity is at a 3½-year high at the same time, so the bank's rate-setters cannot point to a weak economy as a reason to wait. This meeting settles whether that pressure becomes a hike.

boe-2026-12.standing: The Bank of England's nine-member Monetary Policy Committee, which votes eight times a year on Bank Rate. The rate feeds through to British mortgages and business loans, and sterling and gilt yields move with it.
boe-2026-12.recent: The committee votes on the interest rate that British lenders price mortgages and business loans from. The decision settles what borrowing costs households and firms carry into the new year.

boj-2026-12.standing: Japan's central bank, whose policy board meets eight times a year to set the short-term interest rate. Its rate anchors the yen and the cost of the cheap borrowing that funds investments far beyond Japan.
boj-2026-12.recent: Three sources told Reuters the bank is weighing a statement that underlying inflation has roughly reached its 2% target, the shortfall it cited for a decade to keep rates near zero. With that argument gone, the board has to justify holding on other grounds, and the answer reaches the yen and the borrowers worldwide who fund themselves in it.

fred-us-cpi-2026-10-14.standing: The Bureau of Labor Statistics' monthly measure of what US households pay for a fixed basket of goods and services. It steers Federal Reserve rate expectations and Treasury yields, and sets Social Security cost-of-living rises.
fred-us-cpi-2026-10-14.recent: Hiring stalled in September, with 29,000 jobs counted against 90,000 expected, and the Fed is seen skipping an October rate hike. This release is the other half of that argument: it shows whether the energy shock that lifted euro zone inflation to 3.8% has reached US prices while the jobs market weakens.

fred-us-ppi-2026-10-15.standing: The Producer Price Index, published monthly by the Bureau of Labor Statistics, measures what US producers receive for goods and services. It shows cost pressure before it reaches shop prices, and bond yields and the dollar move with it.

fred-us-retail-sales-2026-10-15.standing: The Census Bureau's monthly estimate of what American shops, restaurants and online sellers took in. Consumer spending is about two-thirds of the US economy, so the figure moves growth forecasts, Treasury yields and the dollar.
